stops.note: the bird lives in New Guinea, nearby islands such as Seram, and northern Australia; the Malay name may itself come from a Papuan language
the first Dutch expedition to the East Indies, under Cornelis de Houtman, brought a live cassowary back to Amsterdam in 1597
borrowed from Dutch; Linnaeus later, in 1758, classed it as Struthio casuarius, lumping it in with the ostrich

current_meaning: a large flightless bird of New Guinea and northern Australia with a bony head crest
